observations: Both GDB runs execute original tiny C program, manager creation then synchronous LOCAL device acquisition, then immediate close. No Java/FFM, hooks, attach, supervisor, scheduler, or reaper ownership composition is present.
First run captures PairingBrowser.stop with valid Linux browser, followed by self=NULL, callback frida_fruity_linux_pairing_browser_stop_ready and SIGSEGV.
Second determining run captures local-device acquisition returning before Linux PairingBrowser.start entry. Start and outer stop use same object 0x5555555c1ed0.

At nested null stop, actual DWARF StopData.self=0x5555555c1ed0, _state_=1, _tmp0_=NULL; object ref_count=3 and priv->backend=NULL. Callback is LinuxPairingBrowser stop_ready. This identifies the exact field supplied to the null call.
Fault PC is frida_fruity_pairing_browser_stop+0x1a (library relative 0x65d0e5). RBX and RDI are zero; faulting instruction mov (%rbx),%rdi dereferences saved self.
All-thread stack shows Frida run_main_loop and g_main_loop_run active on worker thread; calling main is waiting inside frida_async_task_execute from frida_device_manager_close_sync.

After diagnostics, GDB continues with original SIGSEGV, program terminates with signal 11; GDB confirms program no longer exists. GDB command itself returns zero; this is successful diagnostic capture, not successful native program behavior.
